model_interpretation.claim: A 32x32 shared tile indexed as tile[row][col ^ row] provides a meaningful alternative to the padded 32x33 scalar layout: it preserves coalesced global loads/stores while avoiding padding, and may avoid shared-memory bank conflicts on a 32-bank organization. Whether its XOR indexing helps on this target versus the padded layout is an empirical question; this candidate alone cannot establish that comparison.

items.subject: Shared-memory transpose layouts and ownership
items.objective: Own only src/candidate.cu. Replace the baseline's strided global stores with a single-pass shared-memory tiled transpose: load input rows coalesced, exchange tile orientation in shared memory, then store output rows coalesced. Compare the padded 32x33 scalar tile with at least one meaningfully different shared-memory layout or multi-element/vectorized thread-ownership variant; do not presume the padded scalar layout is fastest on this target. Measure the complete run at n=1024. Preserve the run entry point and exact bit patterns; produce every C element for every positive n multiple of 32, pass correctness at n=32, 64, 256, and 1024, use no new allocation or other file edits, and report build, correctness, and repeated timing evidence.
